title.narrative: Strengthening responsiveness of health services provision to extreme weather events for urban marginalised people (Urban SHADE)

description.narrative:
General Description Our research aims to improve the preparedness of health services to respond to the needs of the poorest and most marginalised urban residents before, during and after extreme weather events in 10 locations in Sierra Leone, Kenya and India. The health impacts of climate change will be concentrated among the poorest urban populations, particularly the one billion people living in informal settlements. Marginalized urban people are exposed to extreme weather events due to where they live and how they work and are particularly vulnerable to impacts on health and wellbeing due to poor access to services. It has therefore been recognised that the greatest gains in health in the context of climate change will be achieved through reducing the risks faced by the urban poor, including by targeting informal settlements. How to reduce these health risks through strengthened health service delivery which is responsive, equitable and people centred is, however, currently unclear. Access to quality formal healthcare in marginalised urban settings is often limited, especially for certain people such as the elderly and persons with disabilities. Health services are therefore provided by a complex system of formal and informal providers. In extreme weather events including heatwaves and floods, health service delivery is often non-existent, inaccessible, or unaffordable. We will work in equitable partnership with marginalised urban communities and health system providers and managers in India, Kenya and Sierra Leone throughout the research process, in key cities where we have longstanding partnerships and a track record of delivering research and action for improved health and wellbeing. This proposal brings together globally recognised expertise in health systems, urban health, community engagement, participatory research, and climate change. The mixed methods participatory action research is divided into five phases. Phase one will bring together all stakeholders to collaboratively finalise the research design and plans for capacity strengthening, ethics, and safeguarding. Capacity strengthening of all actors including the research team will occur throughout phases two to five. In phase two, we will conduct mixed methods assessments to fill existing data gaps on health impacts, community vulnerabilities and capacities and health service preparedness in each setting. Informed by these assessments, in phase three we will collaboratively design packages of interventions to improve health service provision in extreme weather events. In phase four we will implement and evaluate them. Intervention packages are likely to include utilisation of existing technologies such as mobile phone Last Updated On Oct 31, 2024 10:26 applications and two way information systems. We will monitor, evaluate and share learning within and across settings throughout the project. Phase five focuses on knowledge uptake at the local, national and global levels. This process will create and communicate evidence-based models to improve the responsiveness of health systems and service delivery to extreme weather events.
